title: 数据周报：头部广告投放数据、Arrow 游戏分析、Homescapes 安装量突破 7.74 亿等
content:
Data digest: top ad spender stats, Arrow game analysis, Homescapes hits 774m+ installs, more – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Every Wednesday we break down the latest data, research and financial results into digestible chunks.
Read on for the numbers you need to know about without the fluff.

Sensor Tower reveals ad data for top 15 spenders
The meaty
Sensor Tower report on the state of game advertising
contains a very detailed breakdown of where the top 15 ad spenders in the US are getting the most ad impressions.
Top spender Gossip Harbor gets an overwhelming 51% of its ad impressions through AppLovin, but Scoeply-owned duo Pokémon Go and Monopoly Go each see a higher ad impression share from AdMob – 47% and 31% respectively.
“In-app networks put playable and rewarded formats in front of people already playing casual titles, which is the audience these games need at volume,” says Sensor Tower’s commentary.
It also notes that strategy and 4X games focus on social video, with Kingshot sending 62% of its impressions to YouTube, Facebook and Instagram – Whiteout Survival sends 51% and Raid: Shadow Legends 42% to the same three platforms. Pokémon TCG Pocket, meanwhile, is seeing results on YouTube with 42% of its ad impressions.
Arrow puzzle game downloads peaked in June, IAP revenue continues to rise
The flurry of new ‘arrow puzzle’ games peaked in terms of downloads in June, says a new
AppMagic chart
. While downloads have cooled off for the genre overall, IAP revenue continues to rise, hitting a new high in September (though obviously most of these games monetise by ads).
Miniclip-owned Lessmore and Easybrain are first and third by lifetime downloads with 138m and 87m respectively. Oakever Games / Learnings’ recently-renamed contender Amaze Go, formerly known as Arrows Go, sits in second with 105m lifetime downloads. The top three are way ahead of the rest of the contenders by lifetime revenue.
Homescapes passes 773m installs as it turns nine
To mark the game’s ninth anniversary, Playrix confirmed in a video on
LinkedIn
that Homescapes has been installed 773,485,427 times. The publisher also said that 750k players have been playing for all nine years the game has been available, and there are now over 21k levels in the game. 550k people have completed all 21k stages, Playrix added.
Delta Force passes 58m DAU in China
Tencent’s
Delta Force
has passed 58m daily active users on its China server, up from 50m in March.
Tencent announced the milestone on October 8, as the shooter marked its second anniversary. It launched in September 2024 and passed 12m DAU in April 2025, 20m in July and 30m in September, before reaching 41m in January and 50m in March this year. The firm’s financial report also said the game hit record DAU and revenue over Spring Festival.
Gameloft Q3 revenue up 6% to $80m
Gameloft’s revenue rose 6% year-on-year to $80m (€72m) in Q3, the company said in its recent
financials
. PC and console now account for half of that, leaving mobile making up the other 50%.
The publisher’s top five games by revenue were Disney Dreamlight Valley, Disney Magic Kingdoms, Disney Speedstorm, Asphalt Legends and March of Empires.
Puzzle games lead $1m study with $4.3m median lifetime revenue
According to new data from
AppMagic
, puzzle games that passed $1m in IAP revenue in 2026 have a median lifetime IAP of $4.3m, the highest of any genre with at least five games.
AppMagic looked at 158 games released between January 1 and October 13 that had passed $1m in lifetime IAP revenue by October 17. It excluded 36 games that earn at least half their tracked revenue in China.
The 26 puzzle games took a median of 126 days to reach $1m, the slowest of any genre. RPGs took 62.5 days and have a median lifetime revenue of $2m. Merge 2 and sort puzzle games account for 17 of the 26 puzzle titles and 80% of their combined revenue, with nine merge 2 games on $83.5m and eight sort games on $77.3m.
Of 42 IP-based games, 20 reached $1m within 30 days, against seven of 116 original games. The IP-based games’ median lifetime revenue is $2.6m, against $2m for original titles.
NTE: Neverness to Everness crossed $1m one day after release, and has earned $3.2m in the last 30 days. Jelly Busters took 144 days to get there, but has made $5.8m in the same 30 days.
Nitro Games Q3 revenue down 35% to $1.5m
Nitro Games
reported Q3 revenue of $1.5m (€1.4m), down 35.2% from $2.4m a year earlier. Revenue for the first nine months fell 37.7% to $4.4m.
Game revenue was $0.2m in Q3, against $1.3m from services. EBITDA fell to $82k from $594k, and the company posted an operating loss of $318k and a net loss of $338k.
Nine-month EBITDA of $2m includes a one-off $1.8m gain from the forgiveness of a government-subsidised loan. Without it, EBITDA was about $227k.
Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun Boom launched on mobile at the end of the quarter after 1m pre-registrations, double Nitro’s target. Nitro has also signed a co-publishing deal with Team17 since then.
